decisive_spans.text: A 39-year-old female teacher from Southwest China presented with a subcutaneous mass in the lower-left abdominal region.
The patient had a history of chronic urticaria (relieved by occasional use of loratadine), cesarean section eight years ago, and myomectomy to remove a myoma six months ago.
She denied a history of dysmenorrhea and abortion.
The mass was accompanied by slight pain that worsened around menstruation.
Heart, lungs, and abdomen showed no obvious abnormalities. No palpable swelling of superficial lymph nodes was noted.
A subcutaneous nodule of approximately 1 cm diameter was present under the hypogastrium.
The nodule's surface was normal, without ulceration or bleeding.
A linear scar was observed in the lower-left abdominal region.
Image Description: Showed a hybrid echo-mass about 1.1 × 1.0 cm, with an irregular shape, well-defined border, located 3 mm from the body surface in the subcutaneous soft tissue
Histopathology:    Image Title: Hematoxylin-eosin staining (×40 and ×200)
Image Description: Revealed endometrial glands consisting of a single layer of monomorphous cuboidal cells with an endometrial stroma

response.rationale: The vignette describes a subcutaneous mass near a linear scar in a patient with a history of cesarean section and myomectomy, and histopathology confirmed endometrial glands and stroma. This strongly supports Scar endometriosis. While Subcutaneous Myoma is plausible given the myomectomy history and subcutaneous nodule, the histopathology definitively points to endometriosis.
